input.question: When companies have to cut the 5% of the budget why do a lot of employees get fired? Why can't they just cut 5% of salary from everyone?
input.ground_truth: A company's budget is usually much larger than what they pay everyone. Cutting 5% can amount to far, far more money than 5% of everyone's pay. Not to mention the amount of money most large companies spend on worker's benefits. Usually an employee "costs" more to have than what they're paid. So cutting 5% of their salary will never amount to cutting them out entirely.

Question: When companies have to cut the 5% of the budget why do a lot of employees get fired? Why can't they just cut 5% of salary from everyone?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big cookie jar with cookies for your friends at a playdate. Each friend gets a certain number of cookies to play and have fun.

Now, your grown-up says, “We have to have 5% fewer cookies in the jar.” That means you have to take away a little bit of cookies.

But here’s the thing: if you just take a tiny bit of cookie from each friend’s pile, maybe it’s not enough to make a big difference. Sometimes, the way the playdate works is that each friend needs a certain number of cookies to stay and play. If you don’t have enough cookies for everyone to have what they need, some friends might have to go home early because there aren’t enough cookies for all.

So, instead of giving everyone a little less cookie (which might not be enough to fix the problem), sometimes the grown-ups decide it’s easier to have fewer friends at the playdate. That way, the cookies that are left can go to the friends who stay, and everyone still gets enough to play.

In a company, money is like the cookies. If the company has to have 5% less money, it might not be enough to just give everyone a tiny bit less money. Sometimes, the company needs to pay people to do their jobs, and if there isn’t enough money, they can’t pay everyone. So, they might have to let some people go, so the money they save can go to the people who stay.

But it’s not always fair, and grown-ups in companies try to find the best way to solve the problem.
